title: One of Bolton's most haunted landmarks is closing for winter after Halloween weekend
excerpt: Visitors have one final week to explore Turton Tower before it closes for winter. The 600-year-old manor house, famed for its ghostly legends, shuts on November 1
content:
Visitors have one final week to explore a historic local landmark before it closes its doors for the winter season.

Turton Tower, one of the region's most popular attractions, will close its doors on November 1 before reopening in the spring of 2027.

Given it's reputation as being one of the most haunted places, it is the perfect place to explore on Halloween, which this year falls on a Saturday before it closes at the end of play on Sunday.

The tower has a number of ghostly legends associated with it concerning a lady and 'screaming' skulls.

Turton Tower (Image: NQ)

In 1929, ghost investigator Harry Price documented reports of nightly disturbances at Bradshaw Hall, accounts which later appeared in national newspapers.

While the Tower itself will shut for the winter, visitors will still be able to enjoy the surrounding grounds throughout the colder months.

Turton Tower (Image: NQ)

The Woodland Café will remain open, while the Tower gift shop will continue trading at weekends until Christmas.

A spokesman said: "We now have only one week left of our Summer season, as we close the house to visitors on Sunday 1st November.

"We're open Wednesday to Sunday 11am to 4pm until next weekend so please call in and say hello one last time."

Turton Tower Turton Tower is a beautiful grade 1 listed 600-year-old Tudor Manor House set in extensive gardens and woodlands.

It started life as a medieval stone tower house built in the 1400s and, according to its current custodians, still captures the spirit of a bygone age today.
